Jake, good question — adding more technical detail so your networking team can act. Note: this email is intentionally prescriptive so you can copy/paste during change windows.

1) Egress IPs/CIDRs (Redwood-managed egress gateway)- 
- CSV attached (redwood-egress-cidrs.csv). The list contains three /24 blocks we announce from our egress fleet for the control-plane (all TCP).
- Ports: 443 (HTTPS outbound), 853 (DoT DNS over TLS) if you require DNS tunneling protection, and 123/0udp only if you rely on NTP from our gateway for timing (not required for short-lived flows).

2) mTLS and cert handling- 
- If you select Redwood-managed egress (Option A): we present a Redwood client certificate on egress to upstream partners. For StellarNet's firewall you only need to allow TCP 443 from our three CIDRs and, optionally, accept the client cert if you validate at the reception layer. Redwood will provide the client cert thumbprint and CA chain via a secure artifact (we typically deliver via our vault-backed download or DocuSign for formal handover).
- If you select Customer-managed egress (Option B): Redwood will not present a public egress IP; instead our agents in your VPC will originate to your NAT/proxy. You will terminate TLS there and perform any downstream TLS or mTLS as you prefer. In this model please ensure the NAT preserves source ports (or use SNAT with port mapping) and that connections can be established for long-lived sessions (idle timeout > 15 minutes recommended).

3) Firewall policy guidance (recommended baseline)
- Inbound to customer VPC: allow control-plane agent management on TCP 22 (SSH) or our management plane port (we can provide a port if you prefer non-standard) only from Redwood operator subnets (see CSV).
- Outbound from customer-hosted agents: restrict to our three egress CIDRs on TCP 443 and to your internal DNS/proxy as needed. Avoid wildcard allowlist of 0.0.0.0/0 for egress from sensitive subnets.

4) Logging & audit- 
- If Redwood-managed egress: we supply egress flow logs (sampled) and a weekly summary report for the audit window.
- If Customer-managed egress: ensure your proxy emits connection logs with SNI and TLS fingerprinting for audit ingest. We recommend retaining logs for 90 days as a baseline for SOC-style evidence.

5) Handover checklist for change window (copyable)
- Confirm chosen pattern (Redwood vs customer-managed).
- Apply firewall rules: allow TCP/443 from redwood CIDRs to your ingress endpoints.
- Validate DNS: ensure DNS resolution for redwood-managed hostnames if you choose to allow by hostname.
- Test TLS: run end-to-end curl with client cert validation and capture logs.
- Ops signoff: schedule 30-minute rollback window.

I'll attach the CSV and a simple diagram that maps CIDRs to our egress POPs. If you want, we can run a short smoke test (5–10 minutes) during your maintenance window next Tuesday.
